primary_sources.supports: executescript may implicitly commit a pending transaction; transaction control must be explicit
monotonic clocks do not go backward and are not affected by system clock updates

provenance.deduplication_rule: The previously preserved Generation-204 lease-test flip is not counted again. Gen206 warm-process silence, UnifiedDB transaction closure and GWT telemetry are three different mechanisms; aggregate test growth is supporting context, not independent proof of each mechanism.

evidence: The old warm-process loop used blocking stdout.readline(), so its wall-clock deadline was only checked between lines.
Gen206 gates reads with select(), adds a 25-second first-event deadline, kills silent workers, and opens a 600-second circuit after three silent failures.
The repository narrative reports a 13-minute silent acceptance turn, but the export contains no per-run trace tying the new branch to a bounded browser response.
substantive_delta.residual: Both deadlines still use time.time() rather than a monotonic clock. A system-clock step can lengthen or shorten timeout behavior, and no clock-step test receipt is present.

evidence: The store transaction context now checks Connection.in_transaction before COMMIT or ROLLBACK.
If an inner operation has already committed, successful exit logs and continues; exceptional exit re-raises without rollback because no transaction remains.
Python's sqlite3 documentation states that executescript can implicitly commit a pending transaction, matching the failure class named in the code comments.
The change prevents a completed answer from being discarded by a trailing 'no transaction is active' error, but it cannot restore the atomic boundary after an inner commit.
substantive_delta.credit_boundary: Grant bounded-availability credit only. Do not retain whole-turn or whole-admission atomicity credit for paths that can close the transaction internally until the commit source is removed or isolated and a partial-write falsifier passes.

evidence: UnifiedDB now exports gw_wettbewerb, gw_ausstrahlung and gw_lernen tables plus a broadcast-time index.
The code records candidates separately from emitted articles and stores a lexical/article boost updated from whether Zero's raw answer contains the article id.
Writes are fail-open (exceptions are swallowed), call commit directly and carry no run digest, outcome receipt or uniqueness constraint binding a turn/article observation.
substantive_delta.credit_boundary: This is a falsification and telemetry substrate, not evidence that all global channels compete or that the workspace causally improves outcomes. Keep the existing global-channel, stable-identity/outcome-credit and lexical/evidence-mass tasks OPEN.

hypotheses.claim: If a function closes the UnifiedDB transaction and a later admission step raises, prefix writes remain durable although the turn is reported failed.
hypotheses.falsifier: On an isolated database, inject a deterministic inner executescript/commit after the first admission write and then raise; verify that every turn, workspace, active-turn, memory and graph mutation is absent after failure.

hypotheses.claim: A silent warm worker now yields to the cold path within ERSTE_ZEILE_S plus bounded teardown overhead.
hypotheses.falsifier: A fake worker that keeps stdout open and emits nothing causes answer() or the end-to-end browser turn to exceed the configured first-event deadline, or clock adjustment changes the bound materially.

hypotheses.claim: Separate candidate, emission and learning records make selection pressure and feedback measurable per turn.
hypotheses.falsifier: Reconstructing a frozen turn cannot uniquely join candidates, emitted items, the exact answer, retrieval receipt and downstream outcome, or duplicate/retried writes change the inferred result.

counterhypotheses.claim: All observed inner closures occur only after the complete intended write set, so continuing is an availability repair with no partial-state exposure.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: A fault injected immediately after inner closure leaves any prefix state durable or an active turn orphaned.

counterhypotheses.claim: The 13-minute silence was an external process or environment failure fully handled by first-event detection, not a general timeout defect.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: A worker that emits one event and then stalls still exceeds the overall deadline, or ordinary load triggers false silent-worker classification.

counterhypotheses.claim: The new tables record local lexical selection without reliable provenance or outcome linkage and therefore cannot adjudicate workspace globality or benefit.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: A frozen replay receipt uniquely binds input, candidate identities, emissions, answer citation, channel inventory and an external outcome, and remains invariant under retries.

new_concepts.name: Post-Commit Transaction Shell
new_concepts.definition: A context manager still syntactically surrounds work after an inner operation has already ended the transaction, so the remaining atomicity is representational rather than real.

new_concepts.name: Availability-Atomicity Exchange Rate
new_concepts.definition: A repair preserves the user-visible answer by tolerating a broken transaction boundary; availability improves, but atomicity credit must be explicitly debited until independently restored.

new_concepts.name: Telemetry Without Adjudication
new_concepts.definition: Candidate and emission logs exist, but absent unique provenance and outcome joins they describe activity without proving causal workspace value.

worker_impulses.task: Run TX_INNER_COMMIT_FAULT_MATRIX/v1 on an isolated copy: inject executescript/commit after each admission mutation, then raise at every later boundary. Record before/after table hashes, in_transaction transitions, exact call site and orphaned active-turn count. Remove or isolate every inner transaction closer; do not treat the new log-and-continue branch as atomicity proof.

Run WARM_SILENCE_BOUND/v1 with fake subprocesses: no bytes, partial JSON, one non-result event then silence, EOF, clock step forward/backward and repeated failures across both user pools. Use monotonic deadlines and record warm-to-cold handoff wall time. Preserve all timeouts and false trips.

Add a provenance-preserving GWT trace key binding run/turn, stable native candidate identity, source digest, channel, rank, emitted state, raw-answer citation and downstream outcome. Enforce retry idempotence. Re-run the full channel audit including hyperposition; do not close globality from the three new tables alone.

Record Gen206 as 672/1 with a new source short and preserve the Gen204 red-green lease flip as a separate unresolved family. Award no training, promotion, whole-product PASS, atomicity closure or GWT-globality credit.
